newsitem.title: USA: US Coast Guard sees Houston Channel up later Thurs.
newsitem.headline: US Coast Guard sees Houston Channel up later Thurs.

text.p: The Houston Ship Channel, closed to deep draft vessels due to a capsized barge, should be fully restored by 1600 CDT/2100 GMT, an official in the U.S. Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in Houston said.
"Our hope is it will be reopened by four p.m. Houston time. The capsized vessel is being towed inland," said Lieutenant Elizabeth Becker.

Becker said the ship channel, the maritime artery connecting the Gulf of Mexico with the vast refining and petrochemical infrastructure in the Houston area, said the channel remained open to "towing vessels."
However, other Coast Guard officials clarified that tugs and barges that had cleared the two-mile accident area could continue navigating either way, though no new vessels could enter the zone.
Becker said the two-mile section of the channel near Texas City, midway between Galveston and Houston, was shut at 1032 CDT/1532 GMT.
"It's a slight headache, a low-dose Tylenol," said another Coast Guard official, who said there was no immediate way to determine how many vessels had become backed up because of the shutdown.
Becker said the problem began at 0950/1450 when a deck barge being towed inbound capsized.
She added the barge had been towed away but the Army Corps of Engineers needed to close the accident area to search for two 500-barrel tanks of zinc bromide that were aboard the barge.
She said the chemical did not appear to be a serious threat to aquatic life.
"The concern is a ship could hit the tanks. We want to make the sure the channel is free of the tanks." ((- New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1620))
